title: Renew a lint roller and clean lint off a cloth
instruction: Remove the used outer sheet from the lint roller, then use the fresh layer to clean the lint off the blue cloth.
context: Replacing a saturated sheet restores the tack needed for a roller to pick fibres off clothing. The two-arm sequence combines a counterheld peel from the factory seam with lightly loaded rolling contact across fabric.
setup: A 102 mm wide, 50.8 mm diameter adhesive lint roll on a 28 mm diameter plastic handle rests on two rubber pads, leaving the handle grip accessible from both sides. One used outer sheet is intact, with its perforation toward the robot and its 19 mm low-tack starter zone within reach. A 220 × 218 mm blue felt cloth lies flat with 20 individual pale fibres across a 126 × 65 mm patch. Use the standard YAM station and fixed initial marks.
scoring: 0.30 for completely removing the used sheet while leaving the cloth face up in its work area. Score 0.60 if that is done and at least 10 of the 20 initial tufts are visibly retained on the fresh roll. Score 1.0 if at least 18 are retained and the cleaned cloth stays in its work area for 0.25 s. All other outcomes score 0. Use before-and-after photos of the cloth and roller.
reset_notes: Reinstall a fresh roll with one outer sheet saturated using sacrificial fibres, turn the factory seam toward the arms, set its low-tack corner as shown and reset the cloth with 20 pre-counted tufts.
fidelity: The roller, spindle, starter corner and felt backing have native contacts. A moving peel front and damped opposing tensile load represent flexible adhesive backing. The felt nap applies normal reaction and friction, and loaded rolling transfers the touched tufts to the fresh layer. The unwind threshold is based on published commercial-style lint tape measurements. The corner contact thickness, fabric stiffness and bearing drag are modelling parameters.
scores: Scripted native demo: 1.0. Dream-1: 0 after 480 actions.
